entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Brijesh Kumar Srivastava Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Kamalendra Kumar Maurya Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.
Matter is taken up in the revised call.

By means of this bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.
23 of 2024 at Police Station Saiyan, District Agra under Sections 366, 376 I.P.C.
The applicant is in jail since 13.02.2024.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 19.03.2024.

The following arguments made by Shri Brijesh Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicant,
which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Kamalendra Kumar Maurya, learned counsel for the first informant and Shri Paritosh Kumar Malviya, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant Ankit vs State Of U.P. on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77619810/
1 for grant of bail:
1. The victim and the applicant were intimate and had eloped together.
The couple resided in a hotel.
2. The F.I.R. was lodged after their relationship was exposed and in view of the opposition of the victim's family to the said relationship.
3. The victim in her statements under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. has admitted to intimacy with the applicant.
The victim has stated that she was enticed by the applicant to accompany him to a hotel in Agra.
4. The victim in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. has stated that she was in a relationship with one Virendra @ Veeru and has been blackmailed by the applicant.

5. False and aggravated allegations were made by the victim in the latter part of the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. at the behest of her parents only to deflect attention from her own conduct and save the failing prosecution case.

6. Major inconsistencies in the FIR, the statements under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
discredit the prosecution case.
7. Medical evidence to corroborate commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has not been produced by the prosecution.
8. The victim was never confined or bound down in any manner.
The victim was present at various public places but never raised an alarm nor did she resist the applicant.
The conduct of the victim shows that she was a consenting party.
9. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
10. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant- Ankit be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
Ankit vs State Of U.P. on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77619810/

(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

(iii) The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement passed by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru.
Prin. Secy. Home Deptt. (Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
The learned trial court shall ensure that the right of bail of the applicant granted by this Court is not frustrated by arbitrary demands of sureties, or onerous conditions which are unrelated to the socioeconomic status of the applicant.
